documents.title: Someone at the Gate
documents.tags: Chappaqua Crabtree's Kittle House La Melle Sworn Declaration
documents.summary: A court-ordered exchange at dusk. A blacked-out SUV. Two men in camouflage. A child in the back seat. A court supervisor who filed an affidavit and was removed from the case.

documents.title: The Fool
documents.tags: Origin Privacy Inversion The Fool
documents.summary: A man walks into the Kremlin without credentials during Victory Day. No one stops him. The digital record survived.

documents.title: The Girl on the Boat
documents.tags: Origin Tara Walsh
documents.summary: A boat on the Hudson. A girl in a red-and-white dress holding a chihuahua and a vape pen. She runs a handbag company and a marketing agency. Her clients are all in construction. Her friend got hit by a wrecking ball. So did she.

documents.title: The Bite
documents.tags: Chris Ochoa Origin Tara Walsh
documents.summary: A weekend in the Hamptons. A dinner in white. A dog bite that became a fourth date. Riley the chihuahua was there — packed, planned, present. Three years later, the abuse journal would move Riley back to the city and rewrite every detail of this weekend. The photograph proves otherwise.

documents.title: Tara Knoll
documents.tags: Brendan Walsh Brienne Walsh Chappaqua Family System Interior Moment Maura Walsh Origin Privacy Architecture Tara Knoll Tara Walsh Walsh Sr.
documents.summary: Easter dinner at a house called Tara Knoll — Steve's only visit to the Walsh compound in Chappaqua. Walsh Sr. performs the patriarch. Michael counts change at the table. The sisters wear matching outfits. Brienne watches from a chair. Something about the family is off. He never went back.

documents.title: Nothing Stolen
documents.tags: Documentation Potrero Hill San Francisco
documents.summary: Power cut to one unit. Neighbors still have theirs. The electrical closet forced open, hinges removed. Drill holes in the walls. Nothing stolen. The intrusion itself was the point.

documents.title: The Illness
documents.tags: Discovery Jamie Siminoff Lab Reports Lithium Petrella Poisoning Potrero Hill San Francisco Tom LaFreniere Toxicology
documents.summary: Something is wrong with Steve. Conflicting diagnoses. Tara moves in to take care of him. The symptoms don't match any single explanation. Neither does her attentiveness.

documents.title: The Wine Bottle
documents.tags: Escalation Narrative Inversion Poisoning Potrero Hill Tara Walsh
documents.summary: She threw a wine bottle at his chest. The relationship ends. Or it should have. The breakup has the shape of a Gone Girl exit — perfect victim, perfect villain, nothing quite adding up.

documents.title: The Ultrasound
documents.tags: Evie Narrative Inversion Tara Walsh
documents.summary: She calls months after the breakup. She's pregnant. The baby changes everything — or is supposed to. The reconciliation has the architecture of a con: create the crisis, offer the solution, own the outcome.

documents.title: The Brooklyn Apartment
documents.tags: Brooklyn Chris Ochoa Discovery Don Ackerman Legacy Protection Narrative Inversion Poisoning Tara Walsh
documents.summary: Tara finds an apartment in a mob neighborhood down the street from her sister. She asks Steve to come help look at places for the baby. He goes to the hospital instead. The door closes behind him.

documents.title: The Builder
documents.tags: Bryan Crutcher Jamie Siminoff Aunt K Kinkade Ranch Privacy Inversion San Francisco The Fool Tom LaFreniere
documents.summary: He leaves New York. Gets a driver. Returns to work. Ring is growing — Kleiner money, Ukraine team producing, Amazon watching. Jamie wants more than Steve can give. Prism gets caught in the middle. He meets a woman named Aunt K at a ranch that used to belong to the painter of cottages. For a while, life is normal. Then two catastrophes collide.

documents.title: Eleven O'Clock
documents.tags: Brooklyn Bryan Crutcher Documentation Joe Prendergast Legacy Protection Tamper Screws
documents.summary: Steve flies to New York with his security team ahead of Evie's birth. Tamper screws set to eleven o'clock. NYPD drivers on shift. The birth of his daughter is being planned alongside logistics that have nothing to do with joy.

documents.title: January 27, 2018
documents.tags: Evie Family System Joe Prendergast Legacy Protection Linda Russell Maura Walsh Privacy Architecture Walsh Sr.
documents.summary: Evie is born by emergency C-section. Steve sleeps in a chair for four days. The Walsh family fills the corridors. Then Tara gives him Adderall, and the fog returns.

documents.title: The Painter of Cottages
documents.tags: Jamie Siminoff Aunt K Kinkade Ranch Ring San Francisco
documents.summary: Aunt K comes back. A ranch that belonged to the painter of cottages. Light on the hills. Then Amazon buys Ring, Jamie deletes the options, and Steve files a fourteen-count complaint. Aunt K helps him win.

documents.title: The Morning After
documents.tags: Brooklyn Escalation Legacy Protection Tamper Screws Triangulation Walsh Sr.
documents.summary: He returns to the Brooklyn apartment after four days in a hospital chair. The tamper screws have moved. The air smells wrong. Something adhesive settles on his face. Then Tara and her father arrive and tell him to leave.

documents.title: The Sheraton
documents.tags: Accusation-Reversal Disappearing Record Don Ackerman Legacy Protection
documents.summary: A chaotic sequence of locations after leaving the Brooklyn apartment. Motel 6. A rest stop meeting. An evidence box with items missing. A local officer's warning: don't trust anyone.

documents.title: Terms
documents.tags: San Francisco Tara Walsh Triangulation
documents.summary: Weeks of phone calls from San Francisco to New York. Tara blames her parents. Tara promises cooperation. Tara asks about finances. Then she asks for a private jet.

documents.title: The Jet
documents.tags: Evie Tara Walsh Jesse Matan Gavish Walsh Sr. San Francisco Millennium Tower
documents.summary: A private jet carries Evie from Teterboro to San Francisco. Steve waits at the other end. What he cannot see — what is happening simultaneously in text threads with Jesse, Matan, and Walsh Sr. — is that Tara has planned the exit before the arrival.

documents.title: Save This, I've Got Him
documents.tags: Abby Tedla Narrative Inversion North Beach San Francisco Tara Walsh
documents.summary: A three-level townhouse in North Beach. A nanny. A grandmother. For weeks it feels almost ordinary. Then Tara takes a knife sharpener to Steve's iPhone. Nine marks that look like bullet holes. She photographs a bruise on her thigh and texts her boyfriend. Save this. I've got him.

documents.title: The Leaning Tower
documents.tags: Millennium Tower San Francisco Poisoning Pontius Pilate
documents.summary: Steve moves into a sinking building and goes to the police. The building absorbs its lean internally. So does the investigation.

documents.title: The Niacin Flush
documents.tags: Abby Tedla Discovery Narrative Inversion Poisoning San Francisco Tara Walsh
documents.summary: A wine-and-art event. Two women who walk past the table too many times. Fifteen minutes later, his skin turns red and his body heats up. Tara records the entire episode. He recognizes the feeling from exercise supplements: niacin.

documents.title: She Asked Me to Put Drugs in Your Wine
documents.tags: Abby Tedla Bryan Crutcher Dan Ochoa Discovery Interior Moment Millennium Tower North Beach Poisoning Seroquel Tara Walsh Text Messages
documents.summary: The nanny approaches Steve in the kitchen: 'This will probably get me fired.' She has a brother in the FBI. Her brother told her to tell Steve immediately. The poisoning stops being a suspicion.

documents.title: "You Almost Made Me Abandon Our Daughter"
documents.tags: Abby Tedla Accusation-Reversal Bruises Escalation Evie Matan Gavish Millennium Tower Poisoning Seroquel Tara Walsh Text Messages
documents.summary: A message arrives from Tara. Dramatic, accusatory, the kind of thing she sends often enough that it reads like noise. The phrase about abandoning their daughter is a warning. Steve doesn't recognize it yet.

documents.title: The Uber
documents.tags: Bryan Crutcher Custody Escalation Evie Family System Jesse Matan Gavish Maura Walsh Millennium Tower Tara Walsh Text Messages Walsh Sr.
documents.summary: Three months before the departure, Tara texts a friend asking to be kidnapped. On June 4, 2018, she walks out with Evie and calls an Uber to a bus zone. Bryan Crutcher enters the front passenger seat. The recording captures everything — including Tara telling her father that police will arrest her for poisoning Steve. Walsh Sr. tells her to come home. Then agrees to conditions he later admits, under oath, he was never genuine about. Tara flies to New York and never returns.

documents.title: Crabtree's Kittle House
documents.tags: Abby Tedla Chappaqua Crabtree's Kittle House Custody Delia Farquharson Evie Family System Interior Moment Jason Advocate Jennifer Jackman Judge Gordon-Oliver Katherine Chestnut Aunt K Legacy Protection Maura Walsh Privacy Architecture Supervised Visitation Tara Knoll Walsh Sr. Westchester
documents.summary: A supervised visit after the emergency order. Steve surrenders California jurisdiction over custody to see his daughter. The grandparents bring Evie to a parking lot in Chappaqua. Maura refuses to let go. Walsh Sr. intervenes. The child calms in her father's arms and cries when she sees her grandmother.

documents.title: A Special Relationship
documents.tags: Abby Tedla Chappaqua Corruption Custody Delia Farquharson Elias Gootzeit Evie Family System Jason Advocate Jennifer Jackman Judge Gordon-Oliver Katherine Chestnut Maura Walsh Mount Vernon NY Family Court Pontius Pilate Supervised Visitation Tara Knoll Walsh Sr. Westchester
documents.summary: The court appoints a supervisor who promises integrity and transparency. She meets privately with Tara before the first visit, invites her to attend in violation of the court order, dismisses Steve's concerns about being poisoned, and tells him she has a special relationship with the judge. She charges $250 an hour. The judge who appointed her later admits on the record that she wanted Steve to die on his own sword.

documents.title: Sixteen Visits
documents.tags: Chappaqua Custody Evie Institutional Supervised Visitation Crabtree's Kittle House Walsh Sr. Franceska Anilus Horowitz Disappearing Record Body Speaks Elias Gootzeit Delia Farquharson Mount Vernon Corruption
documents.summary: Sixteen visits. Six supervisors. Every observer reports the same thing: Steve is attentive, Evie is happy. The supervisors keep changing. The reports keep disappearing. The visits stop for five months. The court grants sole custody anyway.

documents.title: The Bruises
documents.tags: Chappaqua Custody Evie Jennifer Jackman Maura Walsh Franceska Anilus Bruises Pontius Pilate Body Speaks Multigenerational Guttridge Forward Evidence
documents.summary: During Visit 15, Steve and two other adults discover bruises on Evie consistent with deliberate injury. Both parents report the bruises as concerning. Tara tells the Attorney for the Child. Steve tells his attorneys, and then the police. Within ten days, the story migrates three times — from concerning to normal to nonexistent — and the court accepts the final version. Months later, Tara's own attorney recuses from the case.

documents.title: The Ambush
documents.tags: Brendan Walsh Chappaqua Claudette LaMelle Documentation Escalation Family System Judge Gordon-Oliver Guttridge La Melle Legacy Protection Privacy Architecture Supervised Visitation Sworn Declaration Tara Knoll Walsh Sr. Westchester Forward Evidence
documents.summary: The last supervised visit ends at dusk. At the gate, a blacked-out SUV. Two men in camouflage. The supervisor who documents what she saw is removed from the case. The judge recuses herself without comment. Steve never sees his daughter again.

documents.title: The Memo
documents.tags: Brienne Walsh Institutional Judge Gordon-Oliver NY Family Court Pontius Pilate Judge Morales-Horowitz Horowitz
documents.summary: Steve files a detailed memorandum describing the ambush, the supervision manipulation, and the historical abuse inside the Walsh household. The court destabilizes. The judge recuses. The case is reassigned.

documents.title: Aunt K
documents.tags: Aunt K StevieLovesEvie Ring Jamie Siminoff Evidence Books
documents.summary: Aunt K is known through the record. She built the blog, compiled the evidence books, and wrote letters to three judges in three months. She helped Steve win the Ring case. She met Evie and became Aunt K. The system that ignored justice also ignored her. She lost a baby to Chappaqua poison.

documents.title: The Reno Bottle
documents.tags: Acute Exposure Aunt K Lab Reports Mycophenolic Acid Poisoning Potrero Hill Reno Tara Walsh Toxicology Vermont Street
documents.summary: Steve recounts illness after sharing a bottle carried from San Francisco to Reno, and the pregnancy loss that followed. He identifies this as his fourth discovery. His separately documented 2019 urine result is distinguished from the bottle analysis and Aunt K's reports, which have not yet been located.

documents.title: Five O'Clock
documents.tags: Custody DiFabio Horowitz Judge Humphrey Aunt K NY Family Court Pontius Pilate Tara Walsh Westchester
documents.summary: Aunt K undergoes surgery days before the hearing. Steve's attorneys request remote appearance at a visitation conference. At the last minute — the afternoon before — the court denies the request. Steve boards an overnight flight. When he arrives, Judge Horowitz has already entered a default — granting permanent custody and a five-year order of protection at what was scheduled as a status conference. Fourteen months later, his motion to vacate is still pending when the third judge recuses.

documents.title: Two Defaults
documents.tags: Custody Institutional Judge Humphrey Aunt K NY Family Court Two Court Systems Pontius Pilate
documents.summary: Steve seeks a Temporary Order of Protection in New York. The TOP is granted. On January 26, 2021, Judge Wayne Humphrey states the fail-to-appear rule on the record — citing Horowitz as precedent. At the evidentiary hearing, Tara and her attorneys fail to appear. Twice. The same judge who announced the rule does not apply it. Humphrey recuses himself — trashing Steve's attorney on the way out. Aunt K investigates the court's own evaluator.

documents.title: Four Discoveries
documents.tags: Abby Tedla Acute Exposure Brooklyn Dan Ochoa Aunt K Lab Reports Lithium Mycophenolic Acid Poisoning Potrero Hill Reno Seroquel Tara Walsh Toxicology Vermont Street
documents.summary: Steve places his four discoveries side by side: the 2017 lithium result, the Brooklyn episode, the nanny’s account and the Reno bottle. The chapter distinguishes the located laboratory reports and testimony from the bottle analysis and paired results still to be found.

documents.title: Equal Threats
documents.tags: Chappaqua DiFabio Family System Judge Humphrey Institutional Judge Schauer Aunt K Linda Russell NY Family Court Two Court Systems Walsh Sr. Westchester Yonkers
documents.summary: The case passes to a fourth judge. Schauer vacates the Horowitz default and issues two temporary orders of protection — one against each party. The poisoner and the poisoned are treated as symmetrical threats. Steve tells the court a permanent temporary order does not give him a chance to face his accuser. The court tells him he is muddying the record.

documents.title: Grandma's Letter
documents.tags: StevieLovesEvie Chappaqua Documentation Evie Aunt K Linda Russell Walsh Sr. Westchester
documents.summary: Steve asks the court to let his mother visit Evie instead. Linda Russell — a retired nurse who raised two sons who attended Stanford — drives thirteen hours round trip to Chappaqua. Walsh Sr. turns her away at the door. She persists. She gets the visits. She writes a letter to Judge Schauer documenting what she sees. Aunt K publishes it on StevieLovesEvie.com.

documents.title: Erase, Deactivate, and Delete
documents.tags: StevieLovesEvie ChappaquaPoison DiFabio Documentation Gag Order Institutional Jennifer Jackman Judge Schauer Aunt K Linda Russell NY Family Court Privacy Inversion Prior Restraint Yonkers
documents.summary: Jennifer Jackman resigns as Attorney for the Child without explanation. Her replacement files a motion to suppress all blog content. A visitation conference is converted into a gag order hearing. Steve is declared in default. Judge Schauer orders the blog removed — every post, every photograph, every grandmother's letter. The words are precise. Erase. Deactivate. Delete.

documents.title: Bora Bora
documents.tags: Custody Gag Order Institutional Interior Moment Jason Advocate Judge Schauer NY Family Court Pontius Pilate Privacy Inversion
documents.summary: His attorney was in the courtroom. He was not. The phone rang after. The voice on the other end sounded beaten. 'Well, that didn't go well.' The orders were final.

documents.title: Orders as Weapons
documents.tags: Brendan Walsh ChappaquaPoison Documentation Gag Order Institutional Narrative Inversion Petrella Walsh Sr.
documents.summary: The court orders leave the courthouse. Tara and the Walsh family circulate them to employers, friends, and journalists — presenting them as proof Steve is dangerous. Reporter Michaelanne Petrella receives a direct threat seventeen days before the gag order exists. Walsh Sr. threatens Steve's attorney by voicemail. The SFPD detective investigating the poisoning is neutralized by a court order hand-delivered by a party to the case.

documents.title: We Were Hit
documents.tags: Brienne Walsh Maura Walsh Walsh Sr. Tara Walsh Deposition Sworn Declaration Trial Two Court Systems Multigenerational
documents.summary: Brienne Walsh wrote publicly about her childhood. In her September 28, 2020 deposition, she said it could be described as abusive, with a qualification: sometimes, not always. Her blog posts, the deposition excerpt and Aunt K’s account are distinct parts of the record.

documents.title: Less Than Genuine
documents.tags: Walsh Sr. Brendan Walsh Maura Walsh Matan Gavish Deposition Aunt K Two Court Systems Attorney Destruction
documents.summary: Three years to arrange. Three days to conduct. Four depositions with one attorney. Coached amnesia, privacy walls, prepared performances — and one unguarded moment from the man who married in. "They were aware of it. They were encouraging it, yeah."

documents.title: The Kidnapping Case
documents.tags: Walsh Sr. Maura Walsh Tara Walsh Attorney Destruction Default
documents.summary: CGC-20-588105. Eight causes of action. Eighty-nine register entries. Three rejected defaults. One family gets the benefit of every procedural doubt. The other gets sanctioned four hundred dollars at a time.

documents.title: The Remnant
documents.tags: Gag Order Prior Restraint Two Court Systems Judge Schauer Jason Advocate Default Westchester
documents.summary: The Second Department rejects the default characterization of the February 2022 order and replaces its blanket deletion command with a narrower directive. The order is affirmed insofar as appealed from. The custody award is not vacated.

documents.title: What Twelve People Saw
documents.tags: Abby Tedla Brienne Walsh Aunt K SF Superior Court San Francisco Tara Walsh Text Messages Trial Two Court Systems Garrett L. Wong
documents.summary: The civil battery case reaches trial in San Francisco Superior Court. A different courtroom. Twelve neutral citizens. The jury hears Steve's account of the nanny's disclosure, Tara's answers, and the documentary evidence.

documents.title: What the Jury Found
documents.tags: SF Superior Court Tara Walsh Trial Two Court Systems Garrett L. Wong
documents.summary: The jury finds battery, domestic violence, and intentional infliction of emotional distress, with a punitive finding of malice, oppression, or fraud. The later judgment records the compensatory damages and costs; the separate punitive award was struck.

documents.title: Affirmed
documents.tags: Two Court Systems Westchester Resolution
documents.summary: Tara appeals the battery verdict. Three arguments. The appellate court finds none of them persuasive. The jury's findings survive review. The judgment is domesticated in the same county where the family court orders remain in effect.

documents.title: The Record Is Open
documents.tags: StevieLovesEvie Documentation Evidence Books Resolution Judge Schauer Westchester
documents.summary: The archive carries the story beyond the verdict and appeals. The 2025–2026 motions, the support-hearing account and the filed Article 78 petition preserve the question Steve asks someone to examine: what should change when the record and the continuing custody arrangement diverge?

documents.title: The Trap
documents.tags: Brendan Walsh Claudette LaMelle Criminalization Architecture Evie Gag Order Judge Gordon-Oliver Judge Morales-Horowitz Tara Walsh Walsh Sr. Westchester
documents.summary: The mechanism that has operated across forty-seven chapters is named. A sleeping photograph sent with conditions attached. A court system that makes silence mandatory. A gate in the dark where the setup is the ambush. A campaign of conditioned photos and impossible terms. Three layers of the same grammar — court-built, physical, ambient — each converting fatherhood into evidence against the father.

documents.title: The Coward
documents.tags: Chappaqua Evie Family System Linda Russell Tara Walsh Walsh Sr. Westchester
documents.summary: A portrait of Stephen Walsh Sr. built from scenes, not diagnosis. The man who confronted a father in a public roadway but retreated from a five-foot-one nanny. Who arranged the ambush but was not in the car. Whose stammer under oath arrived whenever the questioning approached the truth.

documents.title: The Demand
documents.tags: Criminalization Architecture Evie Pontius Pilate Resolution Tara Walsh Walsh Sr. Westchester
documents.summary: After the verdict and the appeal, Tara communicates a new condition — drop the judgment, put money in escrow, stop filing court actions. Contact with Evie becomes conditional on surrendering the legal outcome. When Steve declines, the scheme adapts: forged filings, frozen accounts, threats, displacement.

documents.title: For Evie
documents.tags: Evie Aunt K The Fool
documents.summary: The record becomes the case — the Article 78 filed and unanswered, the federal complaints written and waiting — against a family whose condition has not changed. Too young to understand it now, Evie will need this record: her truth, and a home with an open door.

documents.title: Where Are They Now
documents.summary: A jury returned a verdict. An appellate court corrected the order. The custody arrangement continued. The filed Article 78 petition and unfiled federal drafts carry the record forward, in search of one more person willing to read it and help.

documents.title: Back Cover
documents.summary: Four discoveries. Three substances. Three years. Every person who saw something was removed. A jury heard the evidence. The child is still in Chappaqua.
